    Teleoperation¶

    Operator-side teleoperation stacks: the process an operator runs to stream commands to a robot process. A stack is a TeleopOperator built from a TeleopInputSource (what the operator wears or holds) and a TeleopStreamer (what it sends), configured by TeleopOptions. The stack that ships is SONIC whole-body teleoperation: PICO body tracking on the operator station, sent over ZMQ to the robot process that runs the SONIC policy. The input devices themselves (keyboard, gamepad, SpaceMouse, GELLO, Meta Quest, PICO, Wuji Glove) are on the devices page. The teleoperation guide covers every pipeline and its eden command.

    from eden.extensions.teleop.base import TeleopInputSource, TeleopOperator, TeleopStreamer
from eden.options.extensions.teleop import TeleopOptions

    Base classes and options¶

    Base classes for teleoperation operator stacks.

    The interfaces a teleop stack implements, so future stacks (a different robot, a different tracker, a different wire protocol) share one shape:

    • :class:TeleopOperator — the operator-station lifecycle (setup -> loop -> teardown).
    • :class:TeleopInputSource — a tracked-input device reader.
    • :class:TeleopStreamer — a per-tick pipeline that packs and publishes one message.

    :class:TeleopOperator is the configurable extension object, so it follows the Eden convention shared by every other extension base — ConfigurableMixin bound to a declarative :class:~eden.options.extensions.teleop.TeleopOptions (the same shape as DeploymentBase): its config is mirrored onto the instance from the options, and a concrete stack adds its device-specific parameters as class attributes.

    :class:TeleopInputSource and :class:TeleopStreamer are plain :class:abc.ABC contracts instead, because they are dependency-injected internal components — constructed with live callables and sockets (send, a socket reader), not from a serializable options schema — so ConfigurableMixin (which exists to bind an Options instance) would not fit them. This mirrors sysid's split between SystemIdentificationBase (ConfigurableMixin) and its plain-ABC Excitation interface. The SONIC stack under teleop/sonic is the reference implementation of all three.

    Classes¶

    TeleopInputSource ¶

    Bases: ABC

    A tracked-input device reader (headset / controllers / trackers).

    A concrete source owns a background thread or socket and hands the operator loop the latest sample without blocking. get_latest returns None until the first frame arrives; disconnected reports whether the stream has since gone stale.

    Attributes¶

    disconnected abstractmethod property ¶
    disconnected: bool

    True once the input has gone stale (no fresh frames within the timeout).

    TeleopStreamer ¶

    Bases: ABC

    A per-tick operator pipeline that packs and publishes one wire message.

    A streamer owns one control mode. run_once consumes the latest input and calls the injected send at most once per tick, self-pacing to the mode's rate; its exact arguments are mode-specific, hence the loose signature. reset_yaw re-zeros the accumulated heading on (re)entry and on_mode_exit runs when the mode is left.

    Methods:¶

    Advance one tick: read the latest input and maybe publish one message.

    TeleopOperator ¶

    TeleopOperator(options: T)

    Bases: ConfigurableMixin[TeleopOptions], ABC

    The operator-station lifecycle: build the stack, run the loop, tear down.

    Configured by a :class:~eden.options.extensions.teleop.TeleopOptions (the fields below are mirrored onto the instance by ConfigurableMixin); a concrete stack adds its device-specific parameters as further class attributes. Construct it from an options instance built with configure().

    run is the template method — setup once, then step until should_stop is true, then teardown in a finally (so it runs even on KeyboardInterrupt, which routes through on_interrupt). setup runs inside the same try — it can block for a long time (headset wait) — so teardown must cope with a partially built stack. The loop cadence is set by the streamers' own pacing inside step, not by this loop.

    def __init__(self, options: T) -> None:
    self._uid = gs.UID()
    self._options: T = options

    mirror_options_onto(self, self._options)

    # Deferred, not module-scope — see the NOTE above this module's imports.
    from eden.options._metadata import OPTION_METADATA_KEYS

    # check if there are unused parameters in the options. ``_extra_option_params`` are legitimate
    # options-only fields (not mirrored as attrs), so they are expected to be "unused" here.
    unused_params = set(self._options.keys()) - set(self.get_parameter_names())
    tolerated = {"name", "class_name"} | set(OPTION_METADATA_KEYS) | self._extra_option_params
    # ``params`` is a declared framework field on function-capable term options. An *empty* one is
    # legitimately unused when the same options class configures a class-based term; a non-empty
    # ``params`` on a class-based term would be silently ignored, so it stays invalid.
    if not getattr(self._options, "params", None):
        tolerated.add("params")
    invalid_params = unused_params - tolerated
    if invalid_params:
        # Name the term, not only the class: for a function term the class is the shared
        # ``*FuncWrapper``, which cannot tell the author which of a dozen terms is wrong.
        # Same wording as the construction-time check (``ManagerTermOptions._validate_param_names``).
        term_name = getattr(self._options, "name", None)
        subject = f"term '{term_name}' ({type(self).__name__})" if term_name else type(self).__name__
        raise ValueError(
            invalid_parameters_message(subject, invalid_params, self.get_configure_specs(), self._retired_params)
        )

    def run(self) -> None:
    """Set up the stack, drive the control loop, and tear down on exit."""
    try:
        self.setup()
        while not self.should_stop():
            self.step()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        self.on_interrupt()
    finally:
        self.teardown()

    def __init__(self, **data):
    # Seed type metadata as construction data so BaseModel validates it into
    # __pydantic_extra__ (no-op for extra="forbid" classes, which use
    # the serialization envelope instead).
    data.update(option_metadata(self))
    # NOTE: all of the option modifications/validations should be done in the __init__ method
    try:
        BaseModel.__init__(self, **data)
    except ValidationError as exc:
        # A misspelled field on an extra="forbid" class should teach the field set, not just
        # name the typo. Only rewritten when every error is extra_forbidden.
        enriched = _enrich_extra_forbidden(type(self), exc)
        if enriched is None:
            raise
        raise enriched from None

    SONIC operator station¶

    SONIC operator station: PICO body tracking -> ZMQ commands for the robot process.

    The Eden counterpart of the reference stack's T3. One manager loop polls the controllers, advances the operator state machine, runs the active mode's streamer (POSE at ~50 Hz, planner modes at ~20 Hz), and publishes the command / manager_state messages. Run it with eden teleop sonic operator.

    PICO input arrives through eden pico bridge, which this process spawns (pose-only, port --bridge-port) unless --bridge-host points at an external one or --no-bridge-start is given; --sdk reads the XRoboToolkit SDK in-process instead (the reference-parity path).

    Controls (PICO): A+B+X+Y engage + calibrate (stand in the neutral pose) / stop + exit A+X toggle POSE <-> PLANNER B+Y toggle POSE <-> PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY L-stick click: toggle VR_3PT from either planner mode A+B/X+Y next / previous locomotion mode (planner modes) triggers close/open that hand menu hold pause the pose stream (re-align before releasing)

    Bases: TeleopOperator

    The SONIC operator station as a :class:TeleopOperator.

    setup builds the reader, publish socket, calibration FK, streamers and state machine (blocking until body data arrives); step runs one control tick (poll -> state machine -> effects -> stream -> publish); teardown releases everything, publish socket first. The loop cadence is set by the active streamer's own pacing sleep inside its run_once. Config is mirrored from a :class:~eden.options.extensions.teleop.TeleopOptions (build one with SonicTeleopOperator.configure(**vars(args))); the PICO/SONIC-specific parameters below ride along as options extras.

    def __init__(self, options: TeleopOptions) -> None:
    super().__init__(options)
    self._stop = False
    self._final_command_queued = False  # a planner hand-off is queued: teardown must flush it
    # The robot was handed to the planner and kept its session: it is still engaged, with the
    # heading it captured at the first engage, so the next engage must not reset the facing.
    self._robot_kept_heading = False
    # Built by setup(); None until then, so teardown can release a partial stack.
    self._context = self._socket = self._reader = self._bridge_proc = None
    self._feedback = self._reset_watcher = self._fk = self._viz = self._sm = None

    def setup(self) -> None:
    import genesis as gs
    import zmq

    import eden as en
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.feedback import FeedbackReader, RobotResetWatcher
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.g1_fk import G1KeyFrameFk
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.planner_streamer import PlannerStreamer
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.pose_streamer import PoseStreamer
    from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.three_point import ThreePointPose

    # CPU backend: the calibration FK is a single-env kinematics scene, and
    # the operator pipelines are numpy — claiming a GPU (and torch's default
    # device) here would only fight the robot process.
    en.init(backend=gs.cpu)

    # A --bridge-host bridge runs on another machine, next to its own service.
    self._bridge_proc = None
    if not self.no_service_start and not self.bridge_host and os.path.exists(_SERVICE_SCRIPT):
        subprocess.Popen(["bash", _SERVICE_SCRIPT])
        print(f"[sonic operator] started the XRoboToolkit PC service ({_SERVICE_SCRIPT})")

    if self.sdk:
        from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.inputs import PicoReader

        self._reader = PicoReader()
    else:
        from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.inputs import BridgeReader

        if not self.bridge_host and not self.no_bridge_start:
            # PR_SET_PDEATHSIG is Linux-only; elsewhere the bridge is reaped by teardown alone.
            preexec_fn = _die_with_parent if sys.platform.startswith("linux") else None
            self._bridge_proc = subprocess.Popen(_bridge_argv(self), preexec_fn=preexec_fn)  # noqa: PLW1509
            print(
                f"[sonic operator] started 'eden pico bridge' (pose port {self.bridge_port}, {self.bridge_fps:g} fps)"
            )
        self._reader = BridgeReader(host=self.bridge_host or "127.0.0.1", port=self.bridge_port)
    self._reader.start()

    # Bound before the slow startup (FK compile, headset wait) so a port
    # collision fails fast instead of minutes in. The command socket gets its
    # own context so teardown can term() it — the only call that waits for a
    # queued stop command to be written — without waiting on the feedback /
    # reader sockets that live on the shared instance.
    self._context = zmq.Context()
    self._socket = self._context.socket(zmq.PUB)
    try:
        self._socket.bind(f"tcp://*:{self.port}")
    except zmq.ZMQError as e:
        self._socket.close(linger=0)
        self._context.term()
        self._context = self._socket = None
        raise SystemExit(
            f"[sonic operator] cannot bind tcp://*:{self.port} ({e}) — a previous operator (or the "
            "reference streamer) is still running or still shutting down; stop it, or pass --port"
        ) from e
    print(f"[sonic operator] publishing on tcp://*:{self.port}")

    # Built eagerly, while the headset connects: the first calibration (the
    # engage press) must not stall on the kernel compile.
    print("[sonic operator] building the G1 kinematics scene (first run compiles, up to ~30 s)...")
    self._fk = G1KeyFrameFk()

    print("[sonic operator] waiting for body tracking data (headset in Full-body mode, service WORKING)...")
    while self._reader.get_latest() is None:
        if self._bridge_proc is not None and self._bridge_proc.poll() is not None:
            raise SystemExit(
                f"[sonic operator] the pico bridge exited with code {self._bridge_proc.returncode} — "
                f"check the xrobotoolkit_sdk build and that port {self.bridge_port} is free"
            )
        print("waiting for body data...")
        time.sleep(1)

    on_frame = None
    self._viz = None
    if self.vis_vr3pt:
        from eden.extensions.teleop.sonic.viz import Vr3PtPoseVisualizer

        self._viz = Vr3PtPoseVisualizer(
            with_g1_robot=not self.no_g1,
            enable_waist_tracking=self.waist_tracking,
            enable_smpl_vis=self.vis_smpl,
        )
        on_frame = self._viz.on_frame

    self._three_point = ThreePointPose(self._fk)
    self._feedback = FeedbackReader(host=self.robot_host, port=self.feedback_port)
    self._reset_watcher = RobotResetWatcher(host=self.robot_host, port=self.feedback_port)
    self._pose_streamer = PoseStreamer(
        send=self._socket.send,
        three_point=self._three_point,
        num_frames_to_send=self.num_frames,
        target_fps=self.target_fps,
        record_dir=self.record_dir,
        on_frame=on_frame,
    )
    self._planner_streamer = PlannerStreamer(
        send=self._socket.send, three_point=self._three_point, feedback=self._feedback, on_frame=on_frame
    )
    self._sm = OperatorStateMachine()

    print("[sonic operator] A+B+X+Y engages (stand in the neutral pose: forearms bent 90° forward)")
    print(
        "[sonic operator] A+B+X+Y again disengages: the robot balances in place on the planner; "
        "Ctrl-C exits the operator (the robot keeps idling); end the robot session from its own terminal"
    )
    self._prev_toggle_dc = False
    self._prev_toggle_da = False
    self._bridge_died = False

    def step(self) -> None:
    reader = self._reader
    socket = self._socket
    sm = self._sm

    if self._bridge_proc is not None and not self._bridge_died and self._bridge_proc.poll() is not None:
        self._bridge_died = True
        print(
            f"[sonic operator] WARNING: the pico bridge exited with code {self._bridge_proc.returncode}; "
            "the input stream is frozen — Ctrl-C to exit"
        )
    if input_lost(sm.mode, bridge_died=self._bridge_died, body_stale=reader.disconnected):
        # Frozen input would otherwise leave the robot on the last streamed pose
        # (POSE never times out robot-side) or the last VR 3-point target.
        forced = self._force_off("input lost", "A+B+X+Y re-engages once tracking is back")
        self._release_robot_to_planner(forced.previous)
        return
    controllers = reader.controllers()

    if self._reset_watcher.poll() and sm.mode != StreamMode.OFF:
        self._force_off("robot fell and auto-reset", "stand in the neutral pose and press A+B+X+Y to re-engage")
        self._robot_kept_heading = False  # the reset disengaged the robot: the next engage re-captures it
        return

    transition = sm.step(
        ButtonSnapshot(
            a=controllers.a,
            b=controllers.b,
            x=controllers.x,
            y=controllers.y,
            left_axis_click=controllers.left_axis_click,
            left_menu=controllers.left_menu,
        )
    )

    for effect in transition.effects:
        if effect == Effect.POSE_EXIT:
            self._pose_streamer.on_mode_exit()
        elif effect == Effect.CALIBRATE_FULL:
            sample = reader.get_latest()
            if sample is not None:
                self._three_point.calibrate_now(sample.body_poses)
            else:
                print("[sonic operator] WARNING: no body data available for calibration")
        elif effect == Effect.RESET_POSE_YAW:
            self._pose_streamer.reset_yaw()
        elif effect == Effect.RESET_PLANNER_YAW:
            if transition.previous == StreamMode.OFF and self._robot_kept_heading:
                # The robot stayed engaged on the planner, so it re-captures no heading on
                # this engage: the facing it is idling with must carry over, not snap to forward.
                self._robot_kept_heading = False
            else:
                self._planner_streamer.reset_yaw()
        elif effect == Effect.RELEASE_TO_PLANNER:
            self._release_robot_to_planner(transition.previous)
            print(
                "[sonic operator] disengaged — A+B+X+Y re-engages (full calibration: neutral pose, "
                "looking ahead); Ctrl-C exits the operator"
            )
        elif effect == Effect.SAVE_FROZEN_TARGETS:
            self._planner_streamer.save_upper_body_position_target()
        elif effect == Effect.RECALIBRATE_WRISTS:
            self._planner_streamer.recalibrate_for_vr3pt()

    # Run one tick of the new mode (its pacing sleep sets the loop rate).
    if transition.mode == StreamMode.POSE:
        self._pose_streamer.run_once(reader.get_latest(), controllers)
    elif transition.mode in PLANNER_MODES:
        self._planner_streamer.run_once(
            transition.mode, reader.get_latest(), controllers, reader.get_timestamp_ns()
        )
    else:
        time.sleep(0.005)  # OFF / POSE_PAUSE: idle poll (no hot spin)

    # Command messages go out after the first tick of the new mode, so its
    # data is already in flight when the robot switches.
    if transition.changed:
        print(f"[sonic operator] {transition.previous.name} -> {transition.mode.name}")
        if transition.command is not None:
            kind, planner_flag = transition.command
            socket.send(build_command_message(start=kind == "start", stop=False, planner=planner_flag))

    # manager_state every tick (consumed by data recorders, not the robot).
    toggle_dc_now = controllers.a and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    toggle_da_now = controllers.b and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    socket.send(
        build_manager_state_message(
            stream_mode=transition.mode.value,
            toggle_data_collection=toggle_dc_now and not self._prev_toggle_dc,
            toggle_data_abort=toggle_da_now and not self._prev_toggle_da,
        )
    )
    self._prev_toggle_dc = toggle_dc_now
    self._prev_toggle_da = toggle_da_now

    def teardown(self) -> None:
    if self._socket is not None:
        # Leaving while engaged (Ctrl-C, an exception in step) without the stop
        # combo (which leaves the machine OFF): don't leave the robot holding the
        # last streamed pose.
        if self._sm is not None and self._sm.mode != StreamMode.OFF:
            self._release_robot_to_planner(self._sm.mode)
        # Release the command port first: the viz window and the FK scene can
        # take a while to tear down, and an immediate operator relaunch must not
        # find :5556 still bound to this dying process. linger=0 discards
        # whatever ZMQ has not yet written, though, and the last command is sent
        # microseconds before this — so after one, linger and term() (which
        # blocks until the queue is written or the linger expires) so the robot
        # actually receives it.
        self._socket.close(linger=_FINAL_COMMAND_LINGER_MS if self._final_command_queued else 0)
        self._context.term()
    if self._reader is not None:
        self._reader.stop()
    if self._feedback is not None:
        self._feedback.close()
    if self._reset_watcher is not None:
        self._reset_watcher.close()
    if self._bridge_proc is not None and self._bridge_proc.poll() is None:
        self._bridge_proc.terminate()
        try:
            self._bridge_proc.wait(timeout=3.0)
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            self._bridge_proc.kill()
    if self._viz is not None:
        self._viz.close()
    if self._fk is not None:
        self._fk.close()
    print("[sonic operator] shutdown complete")

    def input_lost(mode: StreamMode, *, bridge_died: bool, body_stale: bool) -> bool:
    """Whether an engaged operator has lost the input its current mode streams from.

    A dead bridge freezes everything. Body staleness only matters to the modes that
    stream body poses: PLANNER / FROZEN_UPPER run on the controllers (whose stalls the
    robot's planner timeout already handles), so a tracker occlusion must not end
    joystick walking.
    """
    if mode == StreamMode.OFF:
        return False
    return bridge_died or (body_stale and mode in _BODY_STREAM_MODES)

    def build_arg_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="eden teleop sonic operator", description="SONIC operator station (PICO body tracking -> robot commands)."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--robot-host", default="localhost", help="Host running 'eden teleop sonic robot' (g1_debug SUB)"
    )
    parser.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=5556, help="Command/planner/pose publish port (bound here)")
    parser.add_argument("--feedback-port", type=int, default=5557, help="Robot g1_debug port")
    parser.add_argument("--target-fps", type=int, default=50, help="Pose stream rate")
    parser.add_argument("--num-frames", type=int, default=5, help="Pose window size (frames per message)")
    parser.add_argument("--record-dir", default="", help="Record each sent pose message as .npz here")
    parser.add_argument("--no-service-start", action="store_true", help="Do not spawn the XRoboToolkit PC service")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--bridge-host",
        default="",
        help="Connect to an 'eden pico bridge' on this host (skips spawning the bridge and the PC service)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--bridge-port",
        type=int,

    parser.add_argument("--no-g1", action="store_true", help="Viz only: hide the G1 mesh")

    def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    args = build_arg_parser().parse_args(argv)
    if args.vis_smpl and not args.vis_vr3pt:
        raise SystemExit("--vis-smpl requires --vis-vr3pt (they share one window)")
    # Every argparse dest is a configurable parameter of the operator, so the
    # namespace maps straight onto TeleopOptions via configure().
    options = SonicTeleopOperator.configure(**vars(args))
    SonicTeleopOperator(options).run()

    Operator state machine for SONIC teleoperation (pure logic, no I/O).

    Port of the reference manager's mode table. Two chains share the VR_3PT sub-mode, which remembers its parent:

    chain 1:  POSE <--(B+Y)--> PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY <--(L-stick click)--> PLANNER_VR_3PT
chain 2:  POSE <--(A+X)--> PLANNER                   <--(L-stick click)--> PLANNER_VR_3PT
VR_3PT --(A+X or B+Y)--> POSE;  A+B+X+Y engages from OFF / disengages from anywhere
POSE --(menu held)--> POSE_PAUSE --(menu released)--> POSE  (level-triggered)

    Button combos are rising-edge except the menu pause. Each transition carries the side effects the manager must run before streaming the new mode's first tick, plus the command message to send after it.

    Disengaging is an Eden deviation: the reference's A+B+X+Y from a live mode sends stop, which ends the robot process — on hardware a damping-only command, and an unsupported robot falls. Here it hands the robot to the planner's IDLE instead, so it keeps balancing in place; the robot session ends only from the robot side.

    def step(self, buttons: ButtonSnapshot) -> Transition:
    """Advance one tick; returns the (possibly unchanged) mode and its effects."""
    ax = buttons.a and buttons.x
    by = buttons.b and buttons.y
    start_combo = buttons.a and buttons.b and buttons.x and buttons.y
    stick = buttons.left_axis_click

    ax_edge = ax and not self._prev_ax
    by_edge = by and not self._prev_by
    start_edge = start_combo and not self._prev_start
    stick_edge = stick and not self._prev_stick

    current = self.mode
    new_mode = current
    if current == StreamMode.OFF:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER
    elif current == StreamMode.PLANNER:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif ax_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE
        elif stick_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT
    elif current == StreamMode.POSE:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif ax_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER
        elif by_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY
        elif buttons.left_menu:  # level, not edge
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE_PAUSE
    elif current == StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif by_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE
        elif stick_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT
    elif current == StreamMode.POSE_PAUSE:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif not buttons.left_menu:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE
    elif current == StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT:
        if start_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.OFF
        elif stick_edge:
            new_mode = self.vr3pt_parent
        elif ax_edge or by_edge:
            new_mode = StreamMode.POSE

    self._prev_ax = ax
    self._prev_by = by
    self._prev_start = start_combo
    self._prev_stick = stick

    transition = Transition(previous=current, mode=new_mode, changed=new_mode != current)
    if transition.changed:
        self._collect_effects(transition)
    self.mode = new_mode
    return transition

    def force_off(self) -> Transition:
    """External force-off (robot fall auto-reset, input loss): back to OFF, no effects but the pose exit.

    The caller decides what the robot needs: nothing after a fall auto-reset
    (it already reset itself), a planner hand-off after an input loss. The
    next A+B+X+Y re-engages through the normal OFF -> PLANNER edge with full
    calibration.
    """
    previous = self.mode
    self.mode = StreamMode.OFF
    transition = Transition(previous=previous, mode=StreamMode.OFF, changed=previous != StreamMode.OFF)
    if previous in (StreamMode.POSE, StreamMode.POSE_PAUSE):
        transition.effects.append(Effect.POSE_EXIT)
    return transition

    PICO body-tracking readers for the SONIC operator station.

    Both readers hand the pipelines the raw XRoboToolkit service data — the (24, 7) full-body joint poses in the service's own frame (positions + scalar-last quaternions) plus controller buttons/sticks/triggers. The SONIC pipelines apply their own frame conversions (see smpl.py / three_point.py), so neither reader goes through :class:eden.utils.devices.pico.xr_client.PicoXrClient's robot-frame poses, whose conversion differs from the reference teleop math.

    :class:BridgeReader (the default) subscribes to eden pico bridge's pose channel and consumes its lossless body_raw passthrough, so the SDK and its service-library linkage live in the bridge process. :class:PicoReader is the in-process port of the reference input_readers.PicoReader: a daemon thread spins on is_body_data_available, dedupes frames by device timestamp, keeps exactly one latest sample, and flags a disconnect after 5 s without fresh data. The bridge reader keeps the same sample semantics (dedupe on the same timestamp, identical dt/fps bookkeeping).

    def __init__(self, host: str = "127.0.0.1", port: int = SONIC_BRIDGE_POSE_PORT) -> None:
    super().__init__()
    # Lazy import: the sonic tests import this module before gating on zmq.
    import zmq

    self._zmq = zmq
    self._sock = zmq.Context.instance().socket(zmq.SUB)
    self._sock.setsockopt(zmq.SUBSCRIBE, b"")
    self._sock.setsockopt(zmq.RCVTIMEO, 100)
    self._sock.setsockopt(zmq.LINGER, 0)
    self._sock.connect(f"tcp://{host}:{port}")
    self._state: dict = {}
    self._thread = threading.Thread(target=self._run, name="sonic-bridge-reader", daemon=True)

    def controllers(self) -> ControllerSample:
    """The latest published controller state (neutral before the first message)."""
    with self._lock:
        state = self._state
    if not state:
        return _NEUTRAL_CONTROLLERS
    lx, ly = state.get("left_thumbstick_value", (0.0, 0.0))
    rx, ry = state.get("right_thumbstick_value", (0.0, 0.0))
    return ControllerSample(
        a=bool(state.get("right_a_button", False)),
        b=bool(state.get("right_b_button", False)),
        x=bool(state.get("left_a_button", False)),
        y=bool(state.get("left_b_button", False)),

    Functions:¶

    POSE-mode streamer: PICO body frames -> 50 Hz windowed SMPL pose messages.

    Port of the reference PoseStreamer. Device frames (~90 Hz) are resampled onto a fixed 50 Hz virtual clock by interpolating between the two frames that bracket each virtual tick (nlerp for rotations), then the last five resampled frames are re-sent as an overlapping window on every tick — the robot's motion merger aligns them by frame index and rides out packet loss. Publishing is gated until the window is full after a mode entry.

    Each message also carries: the wrist joint targets derived from the elbow twist/swing mapping, the calibrated VR 3-point pose of the current frame, Dex3 hand targets from the triggers, data-collection toggle edges, and the right-stick heading increment.

    def update(self, rx: float, dt: float) -> list[float]:
    """Integrate the stick's x-axis; returns the facing unit vector [x, y, 0]."""
    self.dyaw = self.yaw_gain * (-rx) * dt
    if abs(rx) >= self.deadzone:
        self.yaw_angle_rad += self.dyaw
        self.heading = [np.cos(self.yaw_angle_rad), np.sin(self.yaw_angle_rad), 0.0]
    return self.heading

    def __init__(
    self,
    send: Callable[[bytes], None],
    three_point: ThreePointPose,
    fk: SmplFk | None = None,
    num_frames_to_send: int = 5,
    target_fps: int = 50,
    record_dir: str = "",
    on_frame: Callable[[np.ndarray, np.ndarray], None] | None = None,
) -> None:
    """``send`` publishes one packed message; ``on_frame(vr_3pt_pose,
    smpl_joints_local)`` is the visualization hook, called once per
    processed device frame.
    """
    self._send = send
    self._three_point = three_point
    self._fk = fk or SmplFk()
    self._on_frame = on_frame
    self.num_frames_to_send = num_frames_to_send
    self.target_fps = target_fps
    self.record_dir = record_dir
    self._record_idx = 0
    if record_dir:
        import os

        os.makedirs(record_dir, exist_ok=True)

    self.yaw_accumulator = YawAccumulator()
    # 95% of the frame period: the remaining 5% absorbs processing overhead.
    self.frame_time = 0.95 / max(1, target_fps)
    self._sleep = time.sleep

    self.step = 0
    self.frame_buffer: dict[str, deque] = defaultdict(lambda: deque(maxlen=num_frames_to_send))
    self.prev_stamp_ns: int | None = None
    self._last_seen_stamp_ns: int | None = None  # newest device frame run_once has processed
    self.prev_smpl_pose: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.prev_smpl_joints: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.prev_body_quat: np.ndarray | None = None
    self.next_target_ns: int | None = None
    self.frame_start = time.time()

    def run_once(self, sample: BodySample | None, controllers: ControllerSample) -> None:
    """Process the latest device frame; publish when a virtual tick completes."""
    if sample is None:
        self._sleep(0.005)
        return
    if sample.timestamp_ns == self._last_seen_stamp_ns:
        # Same device frame as last tick: every path below would reach the same
        # result again, after a full SMPL-X FK. Without this wait the manager
        # loop would spin between device frames, re-running the FK and publishing
        # manager_state at kHz rates while competing with the reader thread.
        self._sleep(IDLE_POLL_S)
        return
    self._last_seen_stamp_ns = sample.timestamp_ns

    frame = process_body_poses(sample.body_poses, self._fk)
    smpl_pose = frame.body_pose[:63].reshape(21, 3).astype(np.float32)
    smpl_joints = frame.smpl_joints_local.astype(np.float32)
    body_quat = frame.global_orient_quat.astype(np.float32)

    toggle_dc_now = controllers.a and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    toggle_da_now = controllers.b and controllers.left_grip > 0.5
    toggle_dc = toggle_dc_now and not self._toggle_dc_last
    toggle_da = toggle_da_now and not self._toggle_da_last
    self._toggle_dc_last = toggle_dc_now
    self._toggle_da_last = toggle_da_now

    left_hand, right_hand = hand_targets_from_triggers(controllers.left_trigger, controllers.right_trigger)

    # --- resample onto the 50 Hz virtual clock ---
    curr_stamp_ns = sample.timestamp_ns
    step_ns = int(1e9 / max(1, self.target_fps))
    if self.prev_stamp_ns is None:
        self.prev_stamp_ns = curr_stamp_ns
        self.prev_smpl_pose = smpl_pose
        self.prev_smpl_joints = smpl_joints
        self.prev_body_quat = body_quat
        self.next_target_ns = curr_stamp_ns
        return
    if curr_stamp_ns <= self.prev_stamp_ns:
        return  # duplicate device frame
    if self.next_target_ns is None:
        self.next_target_ns = self.prev_stamp_ns + step_ns
    self.next_target_ns = max(self.next_target_ns, self.prev_stamp_ns)
    if self.next_target_ns > curr_stamp_ns:
        return  # virtual tick not yet bracketed
    denom = float(curr_stamp_ns - self.prev_stamp_ns)
    alpha = float(np.clip((self.next_target_ns - self.prev_stamp_ns) / denom if denom > 0 else 1.0, 0.0, 1.0))

    use_joints = (1.0 - alpha) * self.prev_smpl_joints + alpha * smpl_joints
    # Per-joint NLERP of the (21, 3) axis-angle pose, via quaternions.
    prev_q = sRot.from_rotvec(self.prev_smpl_pose.reshape(-1, 3)).as_quat()
    curr_q = sRot.from_rotvec(smpl_pose.reshape(-1, 3)).as_quat()
    use_pose = (
        sRot.from_quat(quat_nlerp(prev_q, curr_q, alpha)).as_rotvec().reshape(smpl_pose.shape).astype(np.float32)
    )
    use_body_quat = quat_nlerp(self.prev_body_quat, body_quat, alpha).astype(np.float32)

    joint_pos = wrist_joints_from_body_pose(use_pose)

    # Calibrated VR 3-point pose of the current (raw) frame.
    vr_3pt_pose = self._three_point.process(sample.body_poses)
    if self._on_frame is not None:
        self._on_frame(vr_3pt_pose, frame.smpl_joints_local)

    self.frame_buffer["smpl_pose"].append(use_pose)
    self.frame_buffer["smpl_joints"].append(use_joints)
    self.frame_buffer["body_quat_w"].append(use_body_quat)
    self.frame_buffer["frame_index"].append(int(self.step))
    self.frame_buffer["joint_pos"].append(joint_pos)

    buffer_is_full = len(self.frame_buffer["frame_index"]) >= self.num_frames_to_send
    if buffer_is_full and self.buffer_cleared:
        self.buffer_cleared = False

    self.yaw_accumulator.update(controllers.right_axis[0], self.frame_time)

    if buffer_is_full and not self.buffer_cleared:
        n = len(self.frame_buffer["frame_index"])
        message_data = {
            "smpl_pose": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["smpl_pose"]),
            "smpl_joints": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["smpl_joints"]),
            "body_quat_w": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["body_quat_w"]),
            "joint_pos": np.stack(self.frame_buffer["joint_pos"]),
            "joint_vel": np.zeros((n, 29)),
            "vr_position": vr_3pt_pose[:, :3].flatten().astype(np.float32),
            "vr_orientation": vr_3pt_pose[:, 3:].flatten().astype(np.float32),
            "frame_index": np.array(self.frame_buffer["frame_index"], dtype=np.int64),
            "left_trigger": np.array([controllers.left_trigger], dtype=np.float32),
            "right_trigger": np.array([controllers.right_trigger], dtype=np.float32),
            "left_grip": np.array([controllers.left_grip], dtype=np.float32),
            "right_grip": np.array([controllers.right_grip], dtype=np.float32),
            "pico_dt": np.array([sample.dt], dtype=np.float32),
            "pico_fps": np.array([sample.fps], dtype=np.float32),
            "timestamp_realtime": np.array([sample.timestamp_realtime], dtype=np.float64),
            "timestamp_monotonic": np.array([sample.timestamp_monotonic], dtype=np.float64),
            "left_hand_joints": left_hand.astype(np.float32),
            "right_hand_joints": right_hand.astype(np.float32),
            "toggle_data_collection": np.array([toggle_dc], dtype=bool),
            "toggle_data_abort": np.array([toggle_da], dtype=bool),
            "heading_increment": np.array([self.yaw_accumulator.dyaw], dtype=np.float32),
        }
        self._send(pack_pose_message(message_data, topic="pose"))
        if self.record_dir:
            import os

            np.savez_compressed(os.path.join(self.record_dir, f"pose_{self._record_idx:06d}.npz"), **message_data)
            self._record_idx += 1

    self.step += 1
    self.next_target_ns += step_ns
    self.prev_stamp_ns = curr_stamp_ns
    self.prev_smpl_pose = smpl_pose
    self.prev_smpl_joints = smpl_joints
    self.prev_body_quat = body_quat

    # Reference parity ([PoseLoop] FPS/Step every 5 s). The resampler emits
    # at most one virtual frame per distinct device sample, so a sustained
    # rate below target means the input path is starving the robot's stream.
    self._emit_count += 1
    now = time.time()
    window = now - self._rate_log_time
    if window >= 5.0:
        rate = self._emit_count / window
        print(f"[PoseLoop] FPS: {rate:.1f} Step: {self.step}")
        if rate < 0.9 * self.target_fps:
            print(
                f"[PoseLoop] WARNING: emitting {rate:.1f} Hz < target {self.target_fps} — "
                "device/bridge rate too low, the robot-side stream will stall"
            )
        self._emit_count = 0
        self._rate_log_time = now

    elapsed = time.time() - self.frame_start
    if elapsed < self.frame_time:
        self._sleep(self.frame_time - elapsed)
    self.frame_start = time.time()

    Functions:¶

    Planner-mode streamer: joystick -> locomotion commands (~20 Hz).

    Port of the reference PlannerStreamer. The left stick sets the movement direction/speed (deadzone-rescaled, rotated into the world by the accumulated facing), the right stick turns, and A+B / X+Y cycle the locomotion mode. PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY attaches the frozen upper-body targets grabbed from the robot's feedback; PLANNER_VR_3PT attaches the calibrated 3-point pose and trigger-driven hand targets.

    def send_idle(self) -> None:
    """Send one IDLE planner message, holding the current facing, with no optional fields.

    No upper-body, hand or VR 3-point fields: the robot reads their absence as "not
    operator-driven", so this drops VR 3-point control (back to the g1 encoder) and the
    frozen upper body. Used when the operator hands the robot back to the planner.
    """
    self._send(
        build_planner_message(
            mode=int(LocomotionMode.IDLE),
            movement=[0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            facing=np.asarray(self.yaw_accumulator.heading),
            speed=-1.0,
            height=-1.0,
        )
    )

    def save_upper_body_position_target(self) -> None:
    """Grab the robot's measured upper body as the frozen targets (retried until it arrives)."""
    self._feedback_pending = None
    if not self.feedback.poll_feedback():
        self._feedback_pending = StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY
        print(

    def recalibrate_for_vr3pt(self) -> None:
    """Schedule wrist recalibration against the robot's measured joints (retried until they arrive).

    Until then no 3-point targets are sent, so the robot keeps the g1 encoder: calibrating
    against an all-zero configuration instead (the arms are not at zero) would produce silently
    wrong wrist offsets and a wrist jump.
    """
    self._feedback_pending = None
    if not self._try_recalibrate_for_vr3pt(quiet=False):
        self._feedback_pending = StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT
        print(
            f"[PlannerStreamer] WARNING: no {_FEEDBACK} for the VR 3PT wrist calibration — 3-point "
            f"targets are held back until it arrives; {_FEEDBACK_HINT}"
        )

    def run_once(
    self, stream_mode: StreamMode, sample: BodySample | None, controllers: ControllerSample, timestamp_ns: int
) -> None:
    """Send one planner command (skipped while the headset stream is stalled)."""
    if timestamp_ns == self._last_timestamp_ns:
        self._sleep(IDLE_POLL_S)  # stalled headset stream: poll, don't spin the manager loop
        return
    self._last_timestamp_ns = timestamp_ns
    self._retry_pending_feedback(stream_mode)

    # A+B -> next mode, X+Y -> previous (rising edges), clamped to the
    # modes the reference exposes (IDLE .. INJURED_WALK).
    ab_now = controllers.a and controllers.b
    xy_now = controllers.x and controllers.y
    if ab_now and not self._prev_ab:
        self.mode = LocomotionMode(min(int(LocomotionMode.INJURED_WALK), int(self.mode) + 1))
        print(f"[PlannerStreamer] mode -> {int(self.mode)}: {self.mode.name}")
    if xy_now and not self._prev_xy:
        self.mode = LocomotionMode(max(int(LocomotionMode.IDLE), int(self.mode) - 1))
        print(f"[PlannerStreamer] mode -> {int(self.mode)}: {self.mode.name}")
    self._prev_ab = ab_now
    self._prev_xy = xy_now

    lx, ly = controllers.left_axis
    rx, _ = controllers.right_axis
    facing = self.yaw_accumulator.update(rx, self.dt)

    raw_mag = float(np.clip(np.hypot(lx, ly), 0.0, 1.0))
    if raw_mag < JOYSTICK_DEADZONE:
        mag, speed = 0.0, -1.0
        mode_to_send = LocomotionMode.IDLE
    else:
        mag = min((raw_mag - JOYSTICK_DEADZONE) / (1.0 - JOYSTICK_DEADZONE), 1.0)
        mode_to_send = self.mode
        if self.mode == LocomotionMode.SLOW_WALK:
            speed = 0.1 + 0.5 * mag  # 0.1 .. 0.6 m/s
        elif self.mode == LocomotionMode.WALK:
            speed = -1.0  # mode default
        elif self.mode == LocomotionMode.RUN:
            speed = 1.5 + 3.0 * mag  # 1.5 .. 4.5 m/s
        else:
            speed = mag

    scale = mag / (raw_mag if raw_mag > 0.0 else 1.0)
    movement_local = np.array([-lx, ly]) * scale
    rotation_facing = np.array([[-facing[1], facing[0]], [facing[0], facing[1]]])
    movement_global = rotation_facing @ movement_local
    movement = [float(movement_global[0]), float(movement_global[1]), 0.0]

    upper_body_position = None
    left_hand = None
    right_hand = None
    if stream_mode == StreamMode.PLANNER_FROZEN_UPPER_BODY:
        upper_body_position = self.feedback.upper_body_position_target
        left_hand = self.feedback.left_hand_position_target
        right_hand = self.feedback.right_hand_position_target

    vr_position = None
    vr_orientation = None
    if stream_mode == StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT:
        if sample is not None and self._feedback_pending != StreamMode.PLANNER_VR_3PT:
            vr_pose = self._three_point.process(sample.body_poses)
            vr_position = vr_pose[:, :3].flatten()
            vr_orientation = vr_pose[:, 3:].flatten()
            if self._on_frame is not None:
                self._on_frame(vr_pose, None)
        left_hand, right_hand = hand_targets_from_triggers(controllers.left_trigger, controllers.right_trigger)

    self._send(
        build_planner_message(
            mode=int(mode_to_send),
            movement=movement,
            facing=np.asarray(facing),
            speed=float(speed),
            height=-1.0,
            upper_body_position=upper_body_position,
            left_hand_position=left_hand,
            right_hand_position=right_hand,
            vr_3pt_position=vr_position,
            vr_3pt_orientation=vr_orientation,
        )
    )

    # ~20 Hz pacing.
    now = time.time()
    sleep_t = self.dt - (now - self._last_send)
    if sleep_t > 0:
        self._sleep(sleep_t)
    self._last_send = time.time()

    Functions:¶

    VR 3-point pose extraction and calibration (VR_3PT mode).

    Port of the reference streamer's 3-point path. From the raw (24, 7) service body frame it takes root (0), left hand (22), right hand (23) and neck (12 — deliberately not the head, which moves too freely), converts them to the robot frame, applies per-joint alignment offsets, and expresses the three keypoints relative to the root. :class:ThreePointPose then calibrates them against G1 forward kinematics so the streamed targets live in the same pelvis-local frame the policy's teleop encoder was trained on:

    • full calibration (every engage): operator stands in the neutral pose == the G1's all-zero joint configuration; the neck orientation and both wrist offsets are captured against FK of q = 0.
    • wrist recalibration (every VR_3PT entry): only the wrist offsets are re-captured, against FK of the robot's measured joints; the neck calibration is preserved to avoid jumps from tracking noise.

    The neck position is never measured: it is reconstructed from the calibrated neck orientation through a fixed two-link chain.

    process ¶

    def calibrate_now(self, body_poses: np.ndarray) -> None:
    """Full calibration against FK of the all-zero joint configuration.

    The operator's neutral pose (upright, feet together, forearms bent 90°
    forward) *is* the G1's zero configuration.
    """
    raw = process_3pt_pose(body_poses)
    # Full means the neck too: it is otherwise captured once and kept across
    # wrist recalibrations, so a re-engage after a fall auto-reset (operator
    # re-donned the headset, or re-ran body calibration) would reuse the first one.
    self._neck_quat_inv = None
    self._override_robot_q = np.zeros(29)
    self._capture_calibration(raw)
    print("[ThreePointPose] calibration completed (zero-pose reference)")

    def process_3pt_pose(body_poses: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Raw ``(24, 7)`` service frame -> ``(3, 7)`` root-relative keypoints.

    Rows are [left wrist, right wrist, neck], each ``[x, y, z, qw, qx, qy, qz]``.
    """
    body_poses = np.asarray(body_poses, dtype=np.float64)
    kp = np.zeros((4, 7))
    for rel_i, joint in enumerate(_KEYPOINT_JOINTS):
        pos, quat = _service_pose_to_robot(body_poses[joint])
        rot = sRot.from_quat(quat, scalar_first=True) * _OFFSETS[rel_i]
        kp[rel_i, :3] = pos
        kp[rel_i, 3:] = rot.as_quat(scalar_first=True)

    root_pos = kp[0, :3].copy()
    root_rot = sRot.from_quat(kp[0, 3:], scalar_first=True)
    for i in range(1, 4):
        kp[i, :3] = root_rot.inv().apply(kp[i, :3] - root_pos)
        kp[i, 3:] = (root_rot.inv() * sRot.from_quat(kp[i, 3:], scalar_first=True)).as_quat(scalar_first=True)
    return kp[1:]

    PICO full-body tracking -> SMPL parameters and root-local joints (POSE mode).

    Port of the reference streamer's SMPL path:

    1. The service's 24 global joint rotations (scalar-last, service frame) become parent-local axis-angle after a per-joint Ry(180°) frame fix.
    2. The root orientation is re-based: pre-multiply Rx(+90°) (service Y-up -> robot Z-up), then post-multiply away SMPL's rest orientation (the 120° rotation about (1,1,1)).
    3. Joint positions come from an SMPL-X forward kinematics over the rest skeleton in sonic/smplx_joints_info.npz (fetched from the Kashu7100/eden_assets HF dataset; 55 joints; output = the 22 body joints
    4. the two thumb tips, SMPL-X indices 39 and 54 — NOT the SMPL left_hand/right_hand joints), expressed in the root-local frame.

    No body-shape (betas) or operator-height scaling exists anywhere in this pipeline — the reference relies on calibration offsets and the policy itself.

    def __init__(self, info_path: str | None = None) -> None:
    info = np.load(info_path or get_asset_path(_SMPLX_INFO_ASSET))
    self._rest_joints = np.asarray(info["J"], dtype=np.float64)  # (55, 3)
    self._parents = np.asarray(info["parents"], dtype=np.int64)  # (55,)
    if self._rest_joints.shape != (55, 3) or self._parents.shape != (55,):
        raise ValueError(f"unexpected SMPL-X skeleton shapes in {info_path}")

    def joints(self, global_orient: np.ndarray, body_pose: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Posed joint positions ``(24, 3)`` for a root axis-angle + 63-dim body pose.

    The full 55-joint pose is ``[global_orient, body_pose, zeros(99)]``;
    the output gathers the 22 body joints plus the two thumb tips.
    """
    body_pose = np.asarray(body_pose, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)[:63]
    full_pose = np.concatenate([np.asarray(global_orient, dtype=np.float64).reshape(3), body_pose, np.zeros(99)])
    rot_mats = sRot.from_rotvec(full_pose.reshape(55, 3)).as_matrix()  # (55, 3, 3)

    rel_joints = self._rest_joints.copy()
    rel_joints[1:] -= self._rest_joints[self._parents[1:]]

    transforms = np.zeros((55, 4, 4))
    transforms[:, :3, :3] = rot_mats
    transforms[:, :3, 3] = rel_joints
    transforms[:, 3, 3] = 1.0

    chain = [transforms[0]]
    for i in range(1, 55):
        chain.append(chain[self._parents[i]] @ transforms[i])
    positions = np.stack(chain)[:, :3, 3]
    return positions[_OUTPUT_JOINTS]

    def global_quats_to_local_aa(body_poses: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Service-frame global joint rotations -> parent-local axis-angle ``(24, 3)``.

    ``body_poses`` is the raw ``(24, 7)`` service array (scalar-last quats).
    Every joint is post-multiplied by ``Ry(180°)`` first (the service's joint
    frames are flipped relative to SMPL's).
    """
    global_quats = np.asarray(body_poses, dtype=np.float64)[:, [6, 3, 4, 5]]
    global_rots = sRot.from_quat(global_quats, scalar_first=True) * sRot.from_euler("y", 180, degrees=True)
    local = []
    for i in range(24):
        parent = SMPL_PARENTS[i]
        rot = global_rots[i] if parent == -1 else global_rots[parent].inv() * global_rots[i]
        local.append(rot.as_rotvec())
    return np.asarray(local)

    def process_body_poses(body_poses: np.ndarray, fk: SmplFk) -> SmplFrame:
    """Full POSE-mode conversion of one raw ``(24, 7)`` service frame."""
    pose_aa = global_quats_to_local_aa(body_poses)
    body_pose = pose_aa[1:].reshape(-1)  # (69,)

    root_quat = sRot.from_rotvec(pose_aa[0]).as_quat(scalar_first=True)
    root_quat = smpl_root_ytoz_up(root_quat)
    global_orient_new = sRot.from_quat(root_quat, scalar_first=True).as_rotvec()

    joints = fk.joints(global_orient_new, body_pose[:63])

    root_quat = remove_smpl_base_rot(root_quat)
    joints_local = sRot.from_quat(root_quat, scalar_first=True).inv().apply(joints)
    return SmplFrame(body_pose=body_pose, global_orient_quat=root_quat, smpl_joints_local=joints_local)

    SMPL elbow/wrist rotations -> G1 wrist joint targets (POSE mode).

    The G1 elbow has a single pitch DOF, so the SMPL elbow's roll/yaw content is decomposed off (twist about the elbow axis vs. swing) and folded into the wrist joints, preserving the SMPL wrist's own rotation. Fills the six wrist entries of the 29-dim IsaacLab joint vector; everything else stays zero on the pose stream.

    def decompose_rotation_aa(rotation_aa: np.ndarray, axis: np.ndarray) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
    """Split axis-angle rotations into twist about ``axis`` and the residual swing.

    Returns wxyz quaternions ``(q_twist, q_swing)`` with ``q = q_twist ⊗ q_swing``
    (:func:`eden.utils.geom.quat_swing_twist` on the rotations' quaternions). A zero
    rotation decomposes into identities (the reference divides by the zero angle there).
    """
    return quat_swing_twist(gu.rotvec_to_quat(np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(rotation_aa, dtype=np.float64))), axis)

    def wrist_joints_from_body_pose(body_pose: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """The 29-dim IsaacLab joint vector for a pose-stream frame (wrists only).

    ``body_pose`` is the frame's ``(21, 3)`` (or flat 63-dim) local axis-angle
    pose. All Euler readings are intrinsic XYZ; the per-side signs follow the
    reference mapping verbatim.
    """
    pose = np.asarray(body_pose, dtype=np.float64).reshape(21, 3)
    joint_pos = np.zeros(29)

    _, l_swing = decompose_rotation_aa(pose[SMPL_L_ELBOW][None], _ELBOW_AXIS)
    _, r_swing = decompose_rotation_aa(pose[SMPL_R_ELBOW][None], _ELBOW_AXIS)
    l_swing_euler = sRot.from_quat(l_swing[:, [1, 2, 3, 0]]).as_euler("XYZ")[0]
    r_swing_euler = sRot.from_quat(r_swing[:, [1, 2, 3, 0]]).as_euler("XYZ")[0]
    l_wrist_euler = sRot.from_rotvec(pose[SMPL_L_WRIST]).as_euler("XYZ")
    r_wrist_euler = sRot.from_rotvec(pose[SMPL_R_WRIST]).as_euler("XYZ")

    l_roll = l_swing_euler[0] + l_wrist_euler[0]
    l_pitch = -l_wrist_euler[1]
    l_yaw = l_swing_euler[2] + l_wrist_euler[2]
    r_roll = -(r_swing_euler[0] + r_wrist_euler[0])
    r_pitch = -r_wrist_euler[1]
    r_yaw = r_swing_euler[2] + r_wrist_euler[2]

    joint_pos[G1_L_WRIST_ROLL] = l_roll
    joint_pos[G1_L_WRIST_PITCH] = -l_pitch  # double negation kept verbatim from the reference
    joint_pos[G1_L_WRIST_YAW] = l_yaw
    joint_pos[G1_R_WRIST_ROLL] = r_roll
    joint_pos[G1_R_WRIST_PITCH] = r_pitch
    joint_pos[G1_R_WRIST_YAW] = r_yaw
    return joint_pos

    Trigger -> Dex3 hand joint targets (the reference's gripper gesture solver).

    There is no Cartesian hand IK: the controller trigger fabricates synthetic fingertip positions (thumb tip fixed, the middle tip snapped onto it when the trigger passes 0.5), and the solver turns thumb-to-finger distances into a gesture choice plus a linear interpolation from the open pose to a preset closed pose. With trigger input only, the result is a binary open/close of the middle-finger power grasp.

    def generate_finger_data(trigger: float, grip: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Synthesize ``(25, 4, 4)`` fingertip transforms from controller inputs.

    The thumb tip sits at x=1; the middle tip joins it when the trigger passes
    0.5 (closing the middle-gesture distance to zero). ``grip`` is accepted
    for interface parity but unused, exactly like the reference.
    """
    del grip
    fingertips = np.zeros((25, 4, 4))
    fingertips[_TIP["thumb"], 0, 3] = 1.0
    if trigger > 0.5:
        fingertips[_TIP["middle"], 0, 3] = 1.0
    return fingertips

    def poll_feedback(self, quiet: bool = False) -> bool:
    """Read the newest robot state (if any) into the target fields.

    Returns whether the measured body configuration arrived. ``quiet`` skips the
    miss message, for callers that retry every tick and report once themselves.
    """
    data = self._poller.get_latest()
    if data is None:
        if not quiet:
            print("[FeedbackReader] no feedback data received")
        self.upper_body_position_target = None
        self.left_hand_position_target = None
        self.right_hand_position_target = None
        self.full_body_q_measured = None
        return False

    body_q = data.get("body_q_measured")
    if body_q is not None:
        full = np.asarray(body_q, dtype=np.float64)
        self.full_body_q_measured = full
        self.upper_body_position_target = full[list(UPPER_BODY_MJ_GATHER)]
    else:
        if not quiet:
            print("[FeedbackReader] body_q_measured not in feedback data")
        self.full_body_q_measured = None
        self.upper_body_position_target = None

    left = data.get("left_hand_q_measured")
    right = data.get("right_hand_q_measured")
    self.left_hand_position_target = None if left is None else np.asarray(left, dtype=np.float64)
    self.right_hand_position_target = None if right is None else np.asarray(right, dtype=np.float64)
    return self.full_body_q_measured is not None

    def poll(self) -> bool:
    """True exactly when a previously-seen ``reset_count`` has increased."""
    data = self._poller.get_latest()
    count = None if data is None else data.get("reset_count")
    if count is None:
        return False
    count = int(count)
    increased = self._last_count is not None and count > self._last_count
    self._last_count = count
    return increased

    G1 key-frame forward kinematics for 3-point calibration (Genesis-backed).

    Computes the poses of the two wrist frames and the torso frame — with the training-time local offsets applied — for a given 29-DOF joint configuration, root fixed at the origin with identity orientation. This is the reference frame the teleop encoder's vr_3point_local_* observations were trained against, so the offsets must match gear_sonic/config/manager_env/commands/terms/motion.yaml exactly.

    The kinematics run on the same Genesis model the robot process simulates (:class:~eden.options.robots.unitree_g1.G1Dofs29Dex3), via a single-env kinematics-only scene (transient_robot_env) held open for the process lifetime. One subtlety: Genesis re-origins the base link onto its inertial frame, so with the FK root at identity the world origin is the solver base frame, not the MJCF pelvis body frame the reference (Pinocchio) uses. The key frames are therefore expressed relative to the pelvis body frame recovered via get_pos/get_quat(relative=True), which cancels the re-origin exactly — pinned against a MuJoCo reference in tests/extensions/teleop/sonic/test_g1_fk.py.

    def __init__(self, robot_options: G1Dofs29Dex3 | None = None) -> None:
    import torch

    from eden.utils.genesis_runtime import transient_robot_env

    self._torch = torch
    self._stack = ExitStack()
    self._env, self._robot = self._stack.enter_context(transient_robot_env(robot_options or G1Dofs29Dex3()))
    robot = self._robot
    if list(robot.dofs_name[:29]) != list(G1_DOFS29_NAME):
        self._stack.close()
        raise ValueError("the FK robot's dofs_name must start with the 29 body joints in MJCF order")
    # Raises (naming the available links) on a miss — same fail-fast as a
    # bad body name in the reference FK.
    _, self._links_idx = self._robot.find_named_links_idx_local([body for body, _ in G1_KEY_FRAMES.values()])
    self._offsets = torch.tensor(
        np.stack([offset for _, offset in G1_KEY_FRAMES.values()]), dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device
    )
    self._n_qs = 7 + len(robot.dofs_name)

    def key_frame_poses(self, q_mj29: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, dict[str, np.ndarray]]:
    """Key-frame poses for a 29-joint configuration (MJCF order, radians).

    Returns ``{key: {"position" (3,), "orientation_wxyz" (4,)}}`` with the
    local offsets folded into the positions.
    """
    from genesis.utils.geom import transform_by_quat

    from eden.utils.geom import subtract_frame_transforms

    torch = self._torch
    q_mj29 = np.asarray(q_mj29, dtype=np.float64).reshape(29)
    qpos = torch.zeros((1, self._n_qs), dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device)
    qpos[0, 3] = 1.0  # free-base identity quaternion (wxyz), root at the origin
    qpos[0, 7:36] = torch.as_tensor(q_mj29, dtype=torch.float32, device=self._env.device)
    self._robot.set_qpos(qpos)  # hands stay at zero; refreshes link poses

    n = len(self._links_idx)
    # relative=True: the MJCF pelvis body frame (the reference's FK root),
    # not the re-origined solver frame the qpos root addresses.
    root_pos = self._robot.get_pos(relative=True)
    root_quat = self._robot.get_quat(relative=True)
    link_pos = self._robot.get_links_pos(ls_idx_local=self._links_idx)[0]
    link_quat = self._robot.get_links_quat(ls_idx_local=self._links_idx)[0]
    rel_pos, rel_quat = subtract_frame_transforms(
        root_pos.expand(n, -1), root_quat.expand(n, -1), link_pos, link_quat
    )
    rel_pos = rel_pos + transform_by_quat(self._offsets, rel_quat)

    return {
        key: {
            "position": rel_pos[i].detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64),
            "orientation_wxyz": rel_quat[i].detach().cpu().numpy().astype(np.float64),
        }
        for i, key in enumerate(G1_KEY_FRAMES)
    }

    Operator visualization: calibrated VR 3-point pose, G1 mesh, SMPL body (PyVista).

    Port of the reference VR3Pt visualizer's rendered content, in one window:

    • the three calibrated keypoints (left wrist light green, right wrist light blue, head orange) as balls with RGB frame triads,
    • the synthesized head chain (origin -> torso offset -> neck along its local Z),
    • a semi-transparent G1 mesh at the origin for spatial reference (geometry from the same MJCF asset the calibration FK loads); with waist tracking the three waist joints follow the calibrated neck orientation,
    • optionally the 24 SMPL joints (lower body blue, upper red) with bones, anchored beside the robot — a pre-engage check that the avatar mirrors the operator.

    Requires pyvista (the sonic-viz extra). The window renders inline on the manager thread, exactly like the reference (visualization costs stream latency; run without --vis-vr3pt for the tightest loop).

    def __init__(
    self,
    with_g1_robot: bool = True,
    enable_waist_tracking: bool = False,
    enable_smpl_vis: bool = False,
    axis_length: float = 0.08,
    ball_radius: float = 0.015,
    robot_opacity: float = 0.4,
    off_screen: bool = False,
) -> None:
    try:
        import pyvista as pv
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(f"--vis-vr3pt needs pyvista: {install_hint('sonic-viz')}") from exc
    self._pv = pv
    self._waist_tracking = enable_waist_tracking
    self._smpl_vis = enable_smpl_vis

    self.plotter = pv.Plotter(window_size=(1100, 850), off_screen=off_screen)
    self.plotter.add_axes()
    self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Plane(i_size=2.0, j_size=2.0), color="lightgray", opacity=0.3)
    for axis, color in zip(np.eye(3), ("red", "green", "blue")):
        self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Line((0, 0, 0), tuple(0.2 * axis)), color=color, line_width=4)

    # VR keypoints: ball + RGB triad each, positioned via the actor matrix.
    self._kp_actors = []
    for color in VR_BALL_COLORS:
        ball = self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Sphere(radius=ball_radius), color=color)
        triad = []
        for axis, axis_color in zip(np.eye(3), ("red", "green", "blue")):
            actor = self.plotter.add_mesh(
                pv.Line((0, 0, 0), tuple(axis_length * axis)), color=axis_color, line_width=3
            )
            triad.append(actor)
        self._kp_actors.append((ball, triad))

    # Synthesized head chain: origin -> torso offset -> neck.
    self._chain = pv.PolyData(np.zeros((3, 3)), lines=np.array([2, 0, 1, 2, 1, 2]), force_float=False)
    self.plotter.add_mesh(self._chain, color="orange", line_width=2)

    self._robot = _G1MeshView(self.plotter, robot_opacity) if with_g1_robot else None

    self._smpl_points = None
    if enable_smpl_vis:
        self._smpl_spheres = []
        for i in range(24):
            color = "steelblue" if i in SMPL_LOWER_BODY else "indianred"
            self._smpl_spheres.append(self.plotter.add_mesh(pv.Sphere(radius=0.02), color=color))
        lines = []
        for i in range(1, 24):
            lines.extend([2, SMPL_PARENTS_VIS[i], i])
        self._smpl_bones = pv.PolyData(np.zeros((24, 3)), lines=np.array(lines), force_float=False)
        self.plotter.add_mesh(self._smpl_bones, color="gray", line_width=2)

    self.plotter.show(interactive_update=True, auto_close=False)

    def on_frame(self, vr_3pt_pose: np.ndarray, smpl_joints_local: np.ndarray | None) -> None:
    """Update the scene for one calibrated ``(3, 7)`` pose (+ optional SMPL joints)."""
    for row, (ball, triad) in enumerate(self._kp_actors):
        mat = _pose_matrix(vr_3pt_pose[row, :3], vr_3pt_pose[row, 3:])
        ball.user_matrix = mat
        for actor in triad:
            actor.user_matrix = mat

    neck_z = sRot.from_quat(vr_3pt_pose[2, 3:], scalar_first=True).apply([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
    torso = np.array([0.0, 0.0, TORSO_LINK_OFFSET_Z])
    self._chain.points = np.stack([np.zeros(3), torso, torso + NECK_LINK_LENGTH * neck_z])

    if self._robot is not None and self._waist_tracking:
        # Waist follows the calibrated neck orientation. as_euler("ZYX")
        # returns [z, y, x] = [yaw, pitch, roll]; the waist joints are
        # yaw (q12), roll (q13), pitch (q14).
        yaw, pitch, roll = sRot.from_quat(vr_3pt_pose[2, 3:], scalar_first=True).as_euler("ZYX")
        q = np.zeros(29)
        q[12], q[13], q[14] = yaw, roll, pitch
        self._robot.set_pose(q)

    if self._smpl_vis and smpl_joints_local is not None:
        points = np.asarray(smpl_joints_local) + _SMPL_ANCHOR
        for i, sphere in enumerate(self._smpl_spheres):
            mat = np.eye(4)
            mat[:3, 3] = points[i]
            sphere.user_matrix = mat
        self._smpl_bones.points = points

    self.plotter.update()
